questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When $n$ identical resistors are connected in series, their equivalent resistance is $n^{2}$ times their equivalent resistance when connected in parallel.
Statement II: When a uniform wire of resistance $R$ is cut into $n$ equal parts and these parts are connected in parallel, the new equivalent resistance of the combination is $\dfrac{R}{n^{2}}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.solution:
Statement I: Let the resistance of each identical resistor be $r$.
In series, the equivalent resistance is $R_{s} = nr$.
In parallel, the equivalent resistance is $R_{p} = \dfrac{r}{n}$.
Taking the ratio, $\dfrac{R_{s}}{R_{p}} = \dfrac{nr}{\left(\dfrac{r}{n}\right)} = n^{2}$.
Thus, $R_{s} = n^{2}R_{p}$. Statement I is correct.

Statement II: When a uniform wire of resistance $R$ is cut into $n$ equal parts, the resistance of each part becomes $r = \dfrac{R}{n}$ (since resistance is directly proportional to length).
When these $n$ parts are connected in parallel, the new equivalent resistance $R_{eq}$ is given by:
$R_{eq} = \dfrac{r}{n} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{R}{n}\right)}{n} = \dfrac{R}{n^{2}}$.
Thus, Statement II is also correct.

Therefore, both statements are correct.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

Assertion : A current flows in a conductor only when there is an electric field within the conductor.
Reason : The drift velocity of electron in presence of electric field decreases.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: In the absence of external electric field, the free electrons move randomly in the conductor, so their drift velocity is zero and therefore there is no current in the conductor. In the presence of electric field, each electron in the conductor experiences a force in a direction opposite to the electric field. Now the free electrons are drifted from negative end to the positive end of the conductor and hence a current starts to flow in the conductor.

questions.solution:

Lengths of sections A P B$ and A Q B$ are $r \theta$ and $r(2 \pi-\theta)$
Resistances of sections A P B$ and A Q B$ are

options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Electric shock is due to the electric current flowing through a living body. When the bird perches on a single high power line, no current passes through its body because its body is at equipotential surface i.e., there is no potential difference. While when man touches the same line, standing bare foot on ground the electrical circuit is completed through the ground. The hands of man are at high potential and his feets are at low potential. Hence large amount of current flows through the body of the man and person therefore gets a fatal shock.

questions.q:
Eels are able to generate current with biological cells called electroplaques. The electroplaques in an eel are arranged in 100 rows, each row stretching horizontally along the body of the fish containing 5000 electroplaques. The arrangement is suggestively shown below. Each electroplaques has an emf of $0.15 \mathrm{~V}$ and internal resistance of $0.25 \Omega$.
The water surrounding the eel completes a circuit between the head and its tail. If the water surrounding it has a resistance of $500 \Omega$, the current an eel can produce in water is about
questions.solution:
In each row all the 5000 electroplaques are connected in series. Therefore, equivalent emf $=0.15 \times 5000=750 \mathrm{~V}$. Equivalent resistance $=0.25 \times 5000=1250 \Omega$. All 100 rows are connected in parallel. Therefore voltage $=750 \mathrm{~V}$. Equivalent resistance $=\frac{1250}{100}=12.50 \Omega$. Thus resultant circuit of eel becomes
Current across $500 \Omega=\frac{V}{R}=\frac{750}{500+12.50}=1.46 \mathrm{~A}$ $I \approx 1.5 \mathrm{~A}$.

Reason : The emf of a dry cell is proportional to its size.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: The electrical force of a cell or battery called electromotive force (emf). This force, which makes electrons flow around a circuit. Each kind of cell has a particular emf. The size of a cell has no effect on its emf. The chemicals in the cell determines its emf, but large cells last longer than small cells of same basic type. This means that from a large cell, we get a particular em $\mathrm{f}$ for more time as compared to small cell.

questions.q: A wire of length $L$ is drawn such that its diameter is reduced to half of its original diameter. If the initial resistance of the wire were $10 \Omega$, its new resistance would be
questions.solution:
Let the original diameter of the wire be $D$. Therefore the new diameter is $D / 2$.
Original area of cross-section is $\frac{\pi D^2}{4}$ and the final area of cross-section is $\frac{\pi D^2}{16}$. The new length of the wire is given by

L $\times \frac{\pi D^2}{4}=$L^{\prime} $\times \frac{\pi D^2}{16} \Rightarrow$L^{\prime}=$\frac{16}{4}$L=4 L

Now, we know that the resistance is given by $R=\rho \frac{L}{A}$.

$\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad$& R^{\prime}=\rho $\frac{L^{\prime}}{A^{\prime}}=\rho \frac{4 L}{A / 4}=$16 R . \\
& {$\left[\because$A^{\prime}=$\frac{\pi D^2}{16}=\frac{A}{4}\right]$} \\
\therefore \quad & R^{\prime}=16 $\times$10=160 \Omega .
\end{aligned}

questions.q: A metal rod consumes power $P$ on passing current. If it is cut into two half and joined in parallel, it will consume power
questions.solution:
Let the resistance of the rod be $R$. If the rod is divided into two equal parts, then each part of the rod will have a resistance of $R / 2$. Now these two parts of the rod are connected in parallel and a voltage $V$ is applied across them. Hence the total power consumed is
$$
P^{\prime}=$\frac{V^2}{R / 2}+\frac{V^2}{R / 2}=$4 $\frac{V^2}{R}=$4 P $\text{$ where }
$ P=\frac{V^2}{R}$ is the power consumed by the original rod when voltage $V$ is applied across it.

questions.q: A current $i$ is flowing through the wire of diameter (d) having drift velocity of electrons $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{d}}$ in it. What will be new drift velocity when diameter of wire is made $\mathrm{d} / 4$ ?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: $N$ lamps each of resistance $r$, are fed by a machine of resistance $R$. If light emitted by any lamp is proportional to the square of the heat produced, prove that the most efficient way of arranging them is to place them in parallel arcs, each containing $n$ lamps, where $n$ is the integer nearest to
questions.solution:
As each are containing $n$ lamps, hence,
Resistance of each arc $=n r$
Number of arcs $=N / n$
Total resistance $S$ is given by
$\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{S} & =\Sigma \frac{1}{n r}=\frac{N}{n}\left(\frac{1}{n r}\right) \\ S & =\frac{n^2 r}{N}\end{aligned}$
$\therefore$ Total resistance $=R+S=R+\left(n^2 r\right) N$
If $E$ is the emf of the machine, current entering the arcs is $E /(R+S)$ and in each arc is $n E /(R+S) N$.
Hence, current passing through each lamp
$I=\frac{n E}{N\left(R+n^2 r / N\right)}=\frac{E}{N}\left[\frac{R}{n}+\frac{n r}{N}\right]^{-1}$
Now, heat produced per second in the lamps is
$H=N_r I^2$
Since, light emitted is proportional to $H^2$ therefore light produced is maximum when $H^2$ and hence $H$ is maximum or $\left[\frac{R}{n}+\frac{n r}{N}\right]$ is minimum. Hence, we can write,
$\frac{R}{n}+\frac{n r}{N}=\left[\left(\frac{R}{n}\right)^{1 / 2}-\left(\frac{n r}{N}\right)^{1 / 2}\right]^2+2\left(\frac{R r}{N}\right)^{1 / 2}$
This is minimum when $\sqrt{R / n}-\sqrt{n r / N}=0$ or very small or $n$ is closely equal to $(N R / r)^{1 / 2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: To reduce the range of voltmeter, its resistance need to be reduced. A voltmeter has resistance $R_0$ and range $V$. Which of the following resistances when connected in parallel will convert it into a voltmeter of range $V / n$ ?
questions.solution:
When a resistance is connected in parallel, it reduces the resistance of combination but the range is not reduced. For the purpose of reducing the range the resistance in series with the galvanometer need to be reduced.
This cannot be achieved by connecting a resistance in parallel with voltmeter. It should be noted that the range of voltmeter can only be increased but cannot be decreased.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: You are given resistance wire of length 50 cm and a battery of negligible resistance. In which of the following cases is largest amount of heat generated?
options: When the wire is connected to the battery directly
When the wire is divided into two parts and both the parts are connected to the battery in parallel.
When the wire is divided into four parts and all the four parts are connected to the battery in parallel.
When only half of the wire is connected to the battery.
questions.solution:
Let $R$ be the resistance of the wire
(a) $H_1=\frac{V^2 t}{R}$
(b) Resistance of each part will be $R$ / 2. When they are connected in parallel, the resistance will be $R / 4$.
Hence, $H_2=\frac{4 v^2 t}{R}$
(c) In case of four wires connected in parallel, the resistance will be $R$ / 8
$\therefore H_3=\frac{8 V^2 t}{R}$
(d) $H_4=\frac{V^2 t}{[R / 2]}=\frac{2 V^2 \cdot t}{R}$
Hence, largest amount of heat will be generated in case of four parts connected in parallel.

questions.q: A rod made up of metal is 1.2 m long and 0.8 cm in diameter. Its resistance is $3.5 \times 10^{-3} \Omega$. Another disc made of the same metal is 2.0 cm in diameter and 1.25 mm thick. What is the resistance between the round faces of the disc?
questions.solution:
Given, $I=12 \mathrm{~m}, d=0.8 \mathrm{~cm}$, $R=3.5 \times 10^{-3} \Omega$, thickness $=1.25 \mathrm{~mm}$, Resistivity of the material of the rod
$\begin{aligned} \rho & =\frac{R A}{I}=\frac{3.5 \times 10^{-3} \times \pi\left(0.4 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2}{1.2} \\ & =46.6 \times 10^{-9} \pi \Omega \mathrm{m}\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & \text{ Resistance of disc, } R=\frac{\rho \text{ (Thickness) }}{\text{ Area of cross-section }} \\ &= \frac{46.6 \times 10^{-9} \pi \times\left(1.25 \times 10^{-3}\right)}{\pi\left(1 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2} \\ &= 5.82 \times 10^{-7} \Omega\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance $25 \Omega$ shows a deflection of 5 divisions when a current of 2 mA is passed through it. If a shunt of $4 \Omega$ is connected and there are 20 divisions on the scale, then the range of the galvanometer is
questions.solution:
There are 20 divisions on scale. Initially, current for 20 divisions $=\frac{2 \times 20}{5}=8 \mathrm{~mA}$
$\begin{array}{ll}\therefore & I g=8 \mathrm{~mA} \\ \because & \frac{I g}{I}=\frac{S}{S+G}\end{array}$
$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad I & =\left(\frac{S+G}{S}\right) I_g \Rightarrow I=\left(\frac{4+25}{4}\right) \times 8 \\ & =29 \times 2=58 \mathrm{~mA}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A wire of resistance $10 \Omega$ is bent to form a complete circle. Find its resistance between two diametrically opposite point.
questions.solution:
The wires $A D C$ and $A B C$ will have resistance $5 \Omega$ each. These two are joined in parallel between $A$ and $C$. The equivalent resistance $R$ between $A$ and $C$ is, therefore given by
$R=\frac{5 \Omega \times 5 \Omega}{5 \Omega+5 \Omega}=2.5 \Omega$

questions.q: Find the resistance of a hollow cylindrical conductor of length 1.0 mm and 2.0 mm respectively. The resistivity of the material is $2.0 \times 10^{-8} \Omega \mathrm{m}$.
questions.solution:
The area of cross-section of the conductor through which charges will be flow is
$\begin{aligned} A & =\pi(20 \mathrm{~mm})^2-\pi(1.0 \mathrm{~mm})^2 \\ & =3 \times \pi \mathrm{mm}^2\end{aligned}$
The resistance of the wire is therefore
$\begin{aligned} R & =\rho \frac{1}{A}=\frac{\left(2.0 \times 10^{-8}\right) \times(10)}{3.0 \times \pi \times 10^{-6}} \\ & =2.1 \times 10^{-3} \Omega\end{aligned}$

Charge flowing in one minute

Charge required to liberate one copper ion 2 C
Number of $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ liberated $=\frac{1.6 \times 60}{2 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}$
$=3 \times 10^{20}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Kirchhoff's law of junction, $\Sigma I=0$, is based on
options: conservation of energy as well as charge
questions.solution: Kirchhoff's first law states that in an electric circuit, the algebraic sum of the currents meeting at any junction in the circuit is zero. i.e., $\quad \Sigma i=0$ Hence, according to Kirchhoff's law $i_1+i_2=i_3+i_4+i_5$ Thus, the sum of currents flowing towards the junction is equal to the sum of the currents flowing away from the junction. In other words, when a steady current flows in a circuit, then there is neither any accumulation of charge at any point in the circuit, nor any charge is removed from there. Thus, Kirchhoff's first law expresses the conservation of charge.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The resistance of an ammeter is $13 \Omega$ and its scale is graduated for a current upto 100 A . After an additional shunt has been connected to this ammeter it becomes possible to measure currents upto 750 A by this meter. The value of shunt resistance is
questions.solution: Let $i_a$ is the current flowing through ammeter and $i$ is the total current. So, a current $i-i_a$ will flow through shunt resistance. Potential difference across ammeter and shunt resistance is same. ie, $\quad i_a \times R=\left(i-i_a\right) \times S$ or $S=\frac{i_a R}{i-i_a}\ldots(i)$ Given, $\quad i_a=100 \mathrm{~A}, i=750 \mathrm{~A}, R=13 \Omega$ Hence, $\quad S=\frac{100 \times 13}{750-100}=2 \Omega$

questions.q: A steady current of 1.5 A flows through a copper voltameter for 10 min . If the electrochemical equivalent of copper is $30 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{C}^{-1}$, the mass of copper deposited on the electrode will be
questions.solution:
If $m$ is the mass of a substance deposited or liberated at an electrode during electrolysis when a charge $q$ passes through electrolyte, then according to Faraday's first law of electrolysis,
or
$\begin{aligned}
& m \propto q \\
& m=z q
\end{aligned}$
where $z$ is a constant of proportionality and is called electrochemical equivalent (ECE) of the the substance.
If an electric current $I$ flows through the electrolyte, then
$\therefore \begin{aligned}
q & =I t \\
m & =z i t
\end{aligned}$
Here,
$\begin{aligned}
i=1.5 \mathrm{~A}, t & =10 \mathrm{~min}=10 \times 60 \mathrm{~s}, \\
z & =30 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{gC}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$
Hence, mass of copper deposited on the electrode
$\begin{aligned}
m & =30 \times 10^{-5} \times 1.5 \times 10 \times 60 \\
& =27 \times 10^{-2}=0.27 \mathrm{~g}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three resistances $P, Q, R$ each of $2 \Omega$ and an unknown resistance $S$ form the four arms of a Wheatstone's bridge circuit. When a resistance of $6 \Omega$ is connected in parallel to $S$ the bridge gets balanced. What is the value of $S$ ?
questions.solution:
The situation can be depicted as shown in figure.

As resistances S and $6 \Omega$ are in parallel their effective resistance is
$\frac{6 S}{6+S} \Omega$
As the bridge is balanced, hence it is balanced Wheatstone's bridge.
For balancing condition,
$\begin{aligned}
& & \frac{P}{Q} & =\frac{R}{\left(\frac{6 S}{6+S}\right)} \\
\text{ or } & & \frac{2}{2} & =\frac{2(6+S)}{6 S} \\
\text{ or } & & 3 S  & =6+S \\
\text{ or } & & S & =3 \Omega
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a metallic wire, the ratio $\frac{V}{i}$ ( $V=$ applied potential difference and $i=$ current flowing) is
options: increases or decreases as temperature rises depending upon the metal
questions.solution:
The resistance of a metallic wire at temperature $t^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is given by
$R_t=R_0(1+\alpha t)$
where $\alpha$ is coefficient of expansion.
Hence, resistance of wire increases on increasing the temperature. Also, from Ohm's law, ratio of $\frac{V}{i}$ is equal to $R$ ie,
$\frac{V}{i}=R$
Hence, on increasing the temperature the ratio $\frac{V}{i}$ increases.

questions.solution: Key Idea : Potential difference across galvanometer should be equal to potential difference across shunt. The shunt and galvanometer are connected as shown in figure. Let total current through the parallel combination is $i$, the current through the galvanometer is $i_g$ and the current through the shunt is $i-i_g$. The potential difference $V_{a b}\left(=V_a-V_b\right) is the same for both paths, so $\begin{array}{ll} & i_g G=$\left(i-i_g\right)$ S \\ $\text{$ or } & i_g(G+S)=i S \\ $\text{$ or } & $\frac{i_g}{i}=\frac{S}{S+G}$\end{array}$ The fraction of current passing through shunt $\begin{aligned} & =$\frac{i-i_g}{i}=1-\frac{i_g}{i} \\ & =1-\frac{S}{S+G}=\frac{G}{S+G}$ \\ & =$\frac{8}{2+8}=\frac{8}{10} \\ & =0.8 \mathrm{~A}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: When a wire of uniform cross-section $a$, length $l$ and resistance $R$ is bent into a complete circle, resistance between two of diametrically opposite points will be

questions.q: A $5 A$ fuse wire can withstand a maximum power of $1 W$ in circuit. The resistance of the fuse wire is
questions.solution:
Power $P=i^2 R$
$\Rightarrow R=\frac{P}{i^2}$
Given, $P=1 \mathrm{~W}, i=5 \mathrm{~A}$
$\therefore R=\frac{1}{(5)^2}=0.04 \Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform wire of length $l$ and having resistance $R$ is cut into $n$ equal parts and all parts are connected in parallel, then the equivalent resistance will be :
questions.solution:
Resistance of each part $R^{\prime}=\frac{R}{n}$
When, these parts are connected in parallel.
Then, $\frac{1}{R^{\prime \prime}}=\frac{1}{R^{\prime}}+\frac{1}{R^{\prime}} \ldots . n$ time
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{n}{R^{\prime}} \\ \therefore \quad R^{\prime \prime} & =\frac{R^{\prime}}{n}=\frac{R}{n^2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a certain current is passed in the circuit as shown in figure, 10 kcal of heat is produced in $5 \Omega$ resistance. How much heat is produced in $4 \Omega$ resistance?
questions.solution:
Heat produced in $5 \Omega=10 \mathrm{kcal}$ Now from the relation. $H_1=i_1^2 R_1 t or i_1^2=\frac{H_1}{R_1 t} or \quad i_1^2=\frac{H_1}{5 t}$ ...(1) Again, $5 \times i_1=10 \times i_2$ or $i_2=\frac{i_1}{2}$
Now heat produced in $4 \Omega$ resistance is $\begin{aligned} H_2 & =i_2^2 R_2 t \\ i_2^2 & =\frac{H_2}{R_2 t}\end{aligned}$ or $\quad \frac{i_1^2}{4}=\frac{H_2}{4 t} or i_1^2=\frac{H_2}{t}$ ...(2) From eqs. (1) and (2) $\begin{aligned} \frac{H_2}{t} & =\frac{H_1}{5 t} \\ \text{$ or $} \quad H_2 & =\frac{H_1}{5}=\frac{10}{2}=2 \mathrm{kcal}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two equal resistances $R$ are joined with voltage source $V$ in (i) series (ii) parallel, the ratio of electrical power consumed in two cases wll be
questions.solution:
(i) In series: total resistance $=R+R=2 R$
Power consumed $P_1=\frac{V^2}{2 R} \quad \ldots$ (i)
(ii) In parallel : potential difference across each resistance will be $V$
So, power consumed in each resistance is
$P=\frac{V^2}{R}$
So total power consumed in two resistance is
$P_2=\frac{V^2}{R}+\frac{V^2}{R}=\frac{2 V^2}{R}$ \quad \ldots$ (ii)
\begin{array}{r}\text{ Hence, required ratio }=\frac{P_1}{P_2}\\ =\frac{V^2 \times R}{2 R \times 2 V^2}=\frac{1}{4}\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The resistance of a galvanometer is $50 \Omega$. When 0.01 A current flows in it, full scale deflection is obtained in galvanometer, the resistance of shunt connected to convert galvanometer into an ammeter of range 5 A , will be
questions.solution:
Here: $I_g=0.01 \mathrm{~A}, G=50 \Omega$
To convert the galvanometer in to an ammeter of range 5 A , a low resistance is to be connected in parallel with coil of galvanometer.
$S=\frac{i g \times G}{i-i_g}$
$=\frac{0.01 \times 50}{5-0.01}=\frac{0.5}{4.99}=0.1 \Omega$

questions.q: When a resistance of $9 \Omega$ is connected at the ends of a battery, its potential difference decreases from 40 V to 30 V. The internal resistance of the battery is
questions.solution:
$E=40 \mathrm{~V}, V=30 \mathrm{~V}, R=9 \Omega$
Internal resistance
$r=\left(\frac{E}{V}-1\right) R=\left(\frac{40}{30}-1\right) 9$
$=\frac{1}{3} \times 9=3 \Omega$

questions.q: The equilvalent resistance and potential difference between $A$ and $B$ for the circuit respectively are
questions.solution:
The equivalent resistance between $A and B$ is
$\frac{1}{R^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{2}{3}$ or $\quad R^{\prime}=\frac{3}{2}=1.5 \Omega$
Now the equivalent resistance between $A and B$ is
$R^{\prime \prime}=1.5+2.5=4 \Omega$
Now by Ohm's law, potential difference between $A and B$ is given by
$\begin{aligned} V_A-V_B & =i R=2 \times 4.0 \\ & =8 \mathrm{volt}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A wire of resistance $R$ is divided in n equal parts, then these parts are joined in parallel, the equivalent resistance of the combination will be
questions.solution:
Resistance of one part $\frac{R}{n}$
Now equivalent resistance of $n$ parts each of resistance $\frac{R}{n}$ in parallel is given by
$R^{\prime}=\frac{R / n}{n}=\frac{R}{n^2}$
